newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Philippines cancels aviation talks with Singapore.
newsitem.headline: Philippines cancels aviation talks with Singapore.

text.p: The Philippines has cancelled two days of aviation talks with Singapore due to begin on Tuesday, a spokeswoman for the Civil Aviation Authority of Singapore (CAAS) said on Monday.
The CAAS said in response to written queries from Reuters that the cancellation was due to other pressing matters that the Philippines Civil Aeronautics Board had to resolve.
Philippines Airlines (PAL) had asked its government over the weekend to delay the talks because of what it said were deficiencies in the Philippine panel's position and pending legal issues.

PAL president and chief operating officer Jose Antonio Garcia, in a letter to Philippine Transportation Secretary Arturo Enrile, asked the government not to enter into any "open skies" aviation pact with Singapore as it would harm national interests.
He said the Philippine negotiating panel had not set clear parameters for the talks despite PAL's appeal for the panel to "take a rationalised approach based on true traffic demand".
Garcia also asked that Victor Limlingan, director of the Philippine Civil Aeronautics Board (CAB), be barred from serving as chairman of the talks.
PAL has sued Limlingan, accusing him of favouring Singapore carriers flying to the Philippines by increasing their passenger capacity last year.
Limlingan has said his action was proper and had been upheld by the CAB.
The CAAS told Reuters the delegations of the two countries had intended to discuss expansion of the Singapore-Philippines air service agreement. It declined to disclose details of the pact.
The CAAS spokeswoman said the Philippines had not indicated when it would be ready to resume talks.
Singapore Airlines, Singapore's national airline, was not immediately available for comment.
